name: Dropbox, Inc.

profile.description: Dropbox provides cloud file backup, sync and sharing, plus adjacent products including Dropbox Sign, DocSend, Reclaim.ai and the AI-powered universal search and knowledge tool Dropbox Dash [3]. Q2 2026 revenue was $631.5M (+0.9% YoY; +1.7% ex-FormSwift, which is being wound down by end-2026), with 18.19M paying users and $2.566B of ARR (+1.0%) [1]. Co-founder Drew Houston announced in May 2026 that he is stepping down as CEO after 19 years to become executive chairman, with product chief Ashraf Alkarmi (ex-Vimeo) succeeding him [4][5]. Aggressive buybacks have cut the weighted diluted share count from 395.8M in 2021 to 226.8M in Q2 2026 and left stockholders' equity negative [3].

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): Over five years Dropbox has broadened beyond sync into e-signature (Sign), DocSend, Reclaim.ai and Dash, but FY2025 revenue of $2.521B was below FY2024's $2.548B, so none of these launches has opened a material new revenue stream [3]. AI Deployment (2/2): Dash, which lets users search and interact with documents, messages, video and audio across multiple apps, is shipping to customers and was cited by Houston as the company's answer to AI disruption [4]. Market Share (1/2): 18.19M paying users and three straight quarters of paying-user growth make Dropbox a meaningful player, but it is no longer the category leader as Microsoft embeds Copilot across OneDrive and 365 [1][5]. Pipeline (0/2): Management has not given dated next-generation products with revenue visibility; FY2026 guidance of $2.513-2.523B implies only ~80bps of ex-FormSwift growth [1]. R&D Intensity (1/1): R&D was 29.3% of TTM revenue, above typical infrastructure-software levels, although absolute R&D fell from $914.9M in 2024 to $732.0M in 2025 [3].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Dropbox's stated mission, to design a more enlightened way of working, is clear and somewhat distinctive, but the founder who articulated it is stepping back from the CEO role in 2026 amid pressure from Google, Apple and Microsoft, so it is not yet proven as institutional DNA [4]. Community Impact (0/2): Public materials describe ESG oversight by a Social Impact and Sustainability team and 2030 carbon-neutrality targets, but the search found no distinctive charitable program with dollar amounts, and the company's own fact sheet says it does not view its ESG goals as material [6][7]. Employee Retention (0/2): Headcount stands at 2,113 and R&D spending fell roughly 20% in 2025, which points to workforce reductions rather than long-tenure retention; no turnover data was found [3]. Insider Buying (0/2): FMP insider statistics show zero open-market purchases against 76 insider sale transactions from Q4 2025 through Q3 2026 [3].

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Calculated mechanically on 7 growth-sleeve metrics (10 weight units): weighted sum 4.59/10, which rounds to 5. Buyback-driven negative equity gives a provider D/E of -181.7% and ROE of -23.5%, so both score 0.0 (ROE carries 2x weight), even though ROIC is a healthy 28.6% [3]. Revenue growth of +0.9% YoY in Q2 2026 scores 0.70, and the 5-year revenue CAGR of 5.7% (FY2020 $1.914B to FY2025 $2.521B) scores 0.71 at 2x weight [1][3]. Forward P/E of 10.9x (derived: the $36.30 price divided by FY2027 consensus EPS of $3.32) scores 1.0. The TTM net margin of 17.5% scores 0.87. The provider's forward PEG of 2.40 scores 0.30 at 2x weight [3]. Liquidity: ~3.98M shares/day × $36.30 ≈ $144M/day, far above the $1M floor.

ai_resilience.label: HIGH RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (4/9, EXPOSED): Investors and analysts have pressed Dropbox on how AI tools from OpenAI and Anthropic could reshape subscription software, and Microsoft has embedded Copilot across OneDrive, Teams and the full 365 suite, which squeezes standalone file storage and search [4][5]. Switching costs and an 18.19M paying base, plus ARR of $2.566B, offer some protection, but growth has already stalled at ~1% [1]. AI Opportunity (0/1): Dash is shipping, but Dropbox has disclosed no quantified AI revenue, and FY2026 guidance implies essentially flat growth [1][4].

infinite_game.summary: Through Sinek's lens, Dropbox has a real cause on paper, but its recent behavior is more finite than infinite. The company has used most of its cash generation to shrink the share count by about 43% since 2021, which pushed equity negative, while revenue went flat and R&D was cut [3]. The founder handing over the CEO role in the middle of an AI-driven competitive squeeze now tests whether 'a more enlightened way of working' outlives him [4][5]. The Dash pivot and the FormSwift wind-down show some willingness to adapt [1].

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): 'Design a more enlightened way of working' is an aspirational, service-oriented cause, but capital allocation has favored buybacks over advancing it, with diluted shares falling from 395.8M in 2021 to 226.8M in 2026 [3]. The cause remains closely tied to Houston personally, and he is now transitioning to executive chairman [4].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): Headcount of 2,113 and a ~20% drop in R&D expense in 2025 point to repeated workforce cuts, and a co-CEO period followed by a founder transition adds organizational uncertainty [3][5]. No evidence of low turnover or exceptional tenure was found.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Public framing of Google, Apple and Microsoft is defensive. Houston has downplayed fears of irrelevance rather than openly using rivals' strengths, such as Copilot's integration, as a learning benchmark [4][5].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Dropbox is repositioning from a storage utility toward Dash-led AI knowledge work and is exiting FormSwift by end-2026 [1][4]. However, the core sync business still generates essentially all revenue, so the shift is incremental rather than transformative.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Winding down FormSwift, which cost about 80-100bps of reported growth, and appointing an outsider product leader as CEO are real near-term sacrifices [1][4]. However, the dominant capital-allocation pattern is financial engineering: debt-funded buybacks drove interest expense from $25.1M in 2024 to $50.0M in Q2 2026 alone [3].

investment_thesis: Bull case: Dropbox is a cash machine. TTM operating cash flow is about 38.7% of revenue, the free-cash-flow yield is 12.1% on a ~$7.9B market cap, and the stock trades at roughly 10.9x FY2027 consensus EPS of $3.32 [3]. Q2 2026 adjusted EPS of $0.75 beat consensus, management raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $2.513-2.523B, and paying users grew for a third straight quarter to 18.19M [1][8]. If Dash lifts ARPU, even modest growth on top of continued share shrinkage could compound per-share earnings.
thesis_continued: Bear case: reported revenue growth is about 1%, constant-currency ex-FormSwift growth was just 0.1% in Q2, and FY2025 revenue actually declined about 1% [1]. Buybacks have left equity negative and doubled interest expense, and Microsoft Copilot and Google bundling are compressing the standalone file-storage category just as the founder steps back from the CEO role [3][4][5]. Without quantified Dash revenue, Dropbox risks becoming a slowly melting annuity.
key_catalysts: Dash monetization: disclosure of attach rates or ARR from Dash bundled into Core plans would show whether AI can re-accelerate ARPU above the current ~1% ARR growth [1]
Completion of the FormSwift wind-down by end-2026, removing a ~80-100bps drag from reported growth in 2027 [1]
Strategic direction under new CEO Ashraf Alkarmi, including any portfolio pruning or M&A after the founder transition [4]
key_risks: Microsoft embedding Copilot across OneDrive, Teams and 365 makes Dropbox's AI search a free feature inside a bundle customers already pay for [5]
Negative stockholders' equity and rising interest expense ($50.0M in Q2 2026 vs $27.3M in Q2 2025) limit flexibility if cash flow weakens [3]
Paying-user churn if AI assistants reduce the need for a separate file-sync subscription; FY2025 revenue already fell ~1% [1]
